title: Local regular equations for a closed immersion of smooth schemes
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $X\to S$ and $Y\to S$ be smooth morphisms [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and let $i:Y\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion over $S$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]. For every $y\in Y$ there are an affine open neighbourhood $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $i(y)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-open-immersion], an integer $b\geq0$ and elements $f_1,\ldots,f_b\in A$ such that $Y\times_XU=\operatorname{Spec}(A/(f_1,\ldots,f_b))$ as a closed subscheme of $U$ [def-pc-base-change], and $f_1,\ldots,f_b$ is an $A$-regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]: multiplication by $f_j$ on $A/(f_1,\ldots,f_{j-1})$ is injective for every $j$, and the final quotient is nonzero.

source.place: Tag 067U, lemma-immersion-smooth-into-smooth-regular-immersion, with regular immersion as in Tag 063J, definition-regular-immersion; the affine regular-equation consequence is used explicitly in more-morphisms.tex Tag 0FUE, lemma-etale-local-structure, first proof paragraph.

proof.text: Fix $y\in Y$ and put $x=i(y)$, $s$ its image in $S$. Choose an affine neighbourhood $W=\operatorname{Spec}R$ of $s$ and an affine open $X_0=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $x$ in the inverse image of $W$. By the affine clause of [def-weil-closed-immersion], $Y_0=Y\times_XX_0=\operatorname{Spec}C$, with $C=A/I$ for an ideal $I\subset A$. Let $\mathfrak q\supset I$ correspond to $x$ and $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak q\cap R$. Both restricted structure morphisms are smooth: a lift against a first-order thickening given by [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] lands in the chosen open because the thickening has the same underlying space; local finite presentation also restricts to opens. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine] to get smooth ring maps $R\to A$ and $R\to C$. In particular $A$ and $C$ are finitely presented over $R$ by [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map], and both are $R$-flat by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-flat].

source.place: Tag 067U, lemma-immersion-smooth-into-smooth-regular-immersion, expanded through Tag 067T, lemma-immersion-lci-into-smooth-regular-immersion, first paragraph; affine reduction in Tag 063W, lemma-fibre-quasi-regular

proof.text: The $R$-algebra $A$ is of finite type, so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-over-finite-type-algebra], applied to $R\to A\to C$, makes $C$ finitely presented over $A$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-surjection-kernel-fg] over $A$ with zero polynomial variables and the quotient surjection $A\to C$. Thus $I=(a_1,\ldots,a_N)$ is finitely generated. This uses no Noetherian hypothesis on $R$ or $A$.

source.place: Tag 00F4, lemma-compose-finite-type, part (4); Tag 00R2, lemma-finite-presentation-independent, n=0; finiteness input to divisors.tex Tag 063W(2)

proof.text: Set $k=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, $\bar A=A\otimes_Rk$, $\bar C=C\otimes_Rk=\bar A/I\bar A$, and let $\bar{\mathfrak q}$ be the point of $\operatorname{Spec}\bar A$ corresponding to $y$ on the fibre. The two local rings $L=\bar A_{\bar{\mathfrak q}}$ and $L/J=(\bar C)_{\bar{\mathfrak q}/I\bar A}$, where $J=I\bar A_{\bar{\mathfrak q}}$, are regular local by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-fibre-regular-local], applied separately to $R\to A$ and $R\to C$. In particular $J$ is proper. By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-quotient-kernel-parameters], choose a minimal generating tuple $z_1,\ldots,z_d$ of the maximal ideal of $L$ such that $J=(z_1,\ldots,z_b)$ for $0\le b\le d$. By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence] this full tuple is regular, hence its first $b$ elements are regular: each multiplication is one of the original injections and every prefix quotient surjects onto the nonzero final quotient.

source.place: Tag 00TT, lemma-characterize-smooth-over-field; Tag 00NR, lemma-regular-quotient-regular; Tag 00NQ, lemma-regular-ring-CM; smooth-fibre specialization of the local argument in divisors.tex Tag 067T

proof.text: Choose $f_j\in I$ whose image in $L$ is a unit multiple of $z_j$. Indeed $L=A_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak pA_{\mathfrak q}$, and $J$ is the image of $I_{\mathfrak q}$, so lift $z_j$ to a fraction $f_j/t_j\in I_{\mathfrak q}$ with $t_j\notin\mathfrak q$. Multiplying each successive generator by the unit $t_j$ preserves its regularity and all prefix ideals. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-quotient-tensor-injective] to $0\to I\to A\to C\to0$ over $R$, with $N=k$ and flat quotient $C$. It identifies $I\otimes_Rk$ with the fibre ideal $I\bar A$. Localizing this exact sequence using [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact] identifies $(I\otimes_Rk)_{\bar{\mathfrak q}}$ with $I_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak p I_{\mathfrak q}$. The images of the $f_j$ generate this module. Therefore for the finite $A_{\mathfrak q}$-module $M=I_{\mathfrak q}/(f_1,\ldots,f_b)A_{\mathfrak q}$ one has $M=\mathfrak pM$, hence $M=\mathfrak qA_{\mathfrak q}M$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators] with the empty generating family to obtain $M=0$. The finite module $I/(f_1,\ldots,f_b)$ consequently vanishes after localizing at $\mathfrak q$. For each generator $a_l$ choose $h_l\notin\mathfrak q$ killing its class in that quotient, and invert $h=\prod_lh_l$. Thus after replacing $A$ by $A_h$ one has $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_b)$ on the entire affine open. The new $A$ remains flat and finitely presented over $R$: localization is exact by the cited lemma, and a presentation for $A_h$ is obtained from one for $A$ by adjoining a variable $u$ and the relation $hu-1$.

proof.text: The fibre algebra $\bar A$ is a finitely generated $k$-algebra: tensor a finite polynomial presentation of $A$ with $k$ and reduce its coefficients. It is therefore Noetherian by [lem-wf-affine-noetherian-components]. The images of $f_1,\ldots,f_b$ form a regular sequence in $L$. Apply [lem-exc-regular-sequence-principal-neighbourhood] to the ring $\bar A$, the prime $\bar{\mathfrak q}$ and these elements. It gives $\gamma\in\bar A\setminus\bar{\mathfrak q}$ on whose principal open the whole tuple is regular. Write $\gamma=a/r$ with $a\in A$ and $r\in R\setminus\mathfrak p$: this is possible since $\bar A=(R\setminus\mathfrak p)^{-1}(A/\mathfrak pA)$. Then $a\notin\mathfrak q$, and replacing $A$ by $A_a$ has precisely the same effect on the fibre. The ideal equality from step 4 persists. Thus the fibre tuple is regular on the whole new fibre, and all $f_j$ vanish at the retained point $y$.

source.place: Tag 061L, lemma-regular-sequence-in-neighbourhood; Noetherianity of finite-type field algebras; spreading step in divisors.tex Tag 063W, lemma-fibre-quasi-regular, first proof paragraph

proof.text: Lift regularity from the fibre by induction on the length of a prefix. The inductive assertion is that, on an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A'$ of $x$ in our current ambient scheme, multiplication by $f_j$ on $A'/(f_1,\ldots,f_{j-1})$ is injective for $j\le e$, and $Z_e=\operatorname{Spec}(A'/(f_1,\ldots,f_e))$ is flat and locally of finite presentation over $W$. For $e=0$ finite presentation follows from step 1 and the localization presentation in step 4, using [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Flatness holds in the stalkwise sense of [def-weil-flat-morphism]: at a prime $\mathfrak r\subset A'$ over $\mathfrak t\subset R$, tensoring an injection of $R_{\mathfrak t}$-modules with $A'_{\mathfrak r}$ is the localization of its tensor with the flat $R$-algebra $A'$, so remains injective by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact]. Suppose $e<b$. In $Z_e$ take the principal closed subscheme $Z_{e+1}=V(f_{e+1})$. Its fibre over $s$ is an effective Cartier divisor near $y$, since the fibre multiplication by $\bar f_{e+1}$ is injective by step 5. Apply [lem-pc-recd-fibre-cartier-local] to $Z_e\to W$, $Z_{e+1}\subset Z_e$ and $y$: the ambient morphism is flat and locally of finite presentation by induction, the closed subscheme is principal, and the stated fibre hypothesis holds. On an open neighbourhood of $y$ in $Z_e$, it makes $Z_{e+1}$ a relative effective Cartier divisor. By [def-pc-relative-effective-cartier], $Z_{e+1}$ is flat over $W$, and its ideal has local nonzerodivisor generators as in [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal]. Choose an ambient principal neighbourhood of $x$ whose intersection with $Z_e$ lies inside that open; this is possible because a closed immersion has the subspace topology and principal opens form a basis in an affine scheme. On this smaller neighbourhood $f_{e+1}$ itself is a nonzerodivisor on $Z_e$: in a stalk write $(f_{e+1})=(v)$ with $v$ a nonzerodivisor, so $f_{e+1}=uv$, $v=w f_{e+1}$; cancellation of $v$ gives $wu=1$, making $u$ a unit. Injectivity on stalks implies injectivity on sections, since a section whose germs all vanish is zero. All earlier injections survive the restriction: if a fraction is killed, multiplying by a power of its denominator reduces to the earlier injection. Finally $Z_{e+1}\to W$ is locally of finite presentation, because its affine presentation is that of $A'$ with the $e+1$ equations $f_j$ adjoined, and every further principal restriction adjoins just a relation $tu-1$. This completes the induction without a Noetherian assumption on the base or ambient ring.

source.place: Tag 063W, lemma-fibre-quasi-regular, first proof paragraph: iterative application of Tag 062Y, lemma-fibre-Cartier, part (3); Tag 062T, definition-relative-effective-Cartier-divisor

proof.text: At $e=b$ let the resulting affine open be $U=\operatorname{Spec}A'$. The ideal identity $I A'=(f_1,\ldots,f_b)$ still holds, so the affine closed-immersion description [def-weil-closed-immersion] identifies $Y\times_XU$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(A'/(f_1,\ldots,f_b))$ as a closed subscheme of $U$. Step 6 gives every successive multiplication injection. Its final quotient has the point $y$ and therefore is nonzero, giving precisely the regular-sequence condition of [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. For $b=0$ step 4 already says that the ideal vanishes on a neighbourhood of $x$; the induction has no steps, and the empty sequence is regular because this neighbourhood contains $y$. Renaming $A'$ as $A$ proves every assertion.
